name: tracker-backup-overwrite
goal: A backup written by another database never replaces or rotates the hub's backups, and backup status checks the newest file on disk

evidence: Repro: a second hub (other db, active host effects, same HOME) writes tracker-<date>.db.gz into the default ~/backups/tracker/native and renames over the live hub's file; live status keeps reporting last_ok from its state file. Writer proven: esqhv8 rig state file last_ok 2026-11-26T17:02:24.871Z size 3094. Expected: another db id never replaces or rotates backups; status checks the file on disk.

tracker-backup.test.ts and trackerBackupFixture only ran one database per backup folder, and status was only read straight after a successful write, never after the file changed. Reusable change: fixture 'sharing' option for a second hub on the same folders; three scenarios in the standard backup test.
loop record red at 191a9d60: bunx vitest run test/services/projects-sessions/tracker-backup.test.ts, 3 failed 6 passed; a foreign db replaced a same-day file (ok:true) and status had no file check.

assertTrackerBackupOwner: newest daily and every file about to be replaced must carry this db id (unreadable fails closed), before rename. status.file_error checks last_ok_file presence and size; stale and health fail; one alert.
